intro: STL to 3MF converts 3D models from STL to 3MF on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to store a part with its real units so the slicer does not open it ten times smaller or bigger. 3MF is the modern 3D printing format: a ZIP with the model in XML that stores units, several named parts and the colour of each face, opened directly by PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Cura and Windows.

STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours, as text (ASCII) or binary. STL does not store units and is taken as millimetres, the usual case; if your model was drawn in centimetres, metres or inches, say so and the conversion turns it into the units you want for the 3MF. You can also apply a scale, for example 0.5 to print the STL at half size.

Each face's colours are stored in the 3MF as a colour group, and each part keeps its name, so you can pick each one's filament in the slicer. If the STL has several parts, you can keep them separate inside the 3MF when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The geometry is not simplified or repaired: every triangle of the STL reaches the 3MF unchanged, with duplicate vertices merged. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, checked before the file is processed. Files are deleted automatically when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more STL files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does my STL come out tiny or huge?
faq.a: Because the target program assumes other units. Set the units of the original and of the 3MF.
No: the 3MF has exactly the same geometry. To close holes or fix normals, use Repair STL.
Up to ten STL files per task, with a ZIP of all the 3MF files at the end.
